newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Metals-Industrial users watch LME trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian Metals-Industrial users watch LME trends.

text.p: Indian industrial consumers are watching the movement of copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) before placing orders with local stockists, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Industrial consumers are hoping that copper prices will fall further on the LME," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange.
"Besides, there's a poor offtake of copper in the local market because of a downtrend in industrial activity in general."
"The market is weak and will continue to be subdued in the next few days," said Parikh. Copper prices fell 175 rupees to 13,700 rupees per quintal in the week to Wednesday.
"A revival in demand is not in sight even when prices are down," said Parikh. "But prices will rise if the LME firms."
Dealers said state-run Hindustan Copper Ltd had not revised its prices down despite a drop in LME prices.
India imports all non-ferrous metals with the exception of aluminium. The movement of LME prices has a direct bearing on Indian market trends.

In the week to Wednesday, tin and nickel dropped 600 rupees and 400 rupees per quintal (100 kg) to 29,200 rupees and 34,100 rupees respectively. Last week, nickel and tin lost 900 rupees and 600 rupees per quintal respectively.
Zinc fell 50 rupees to 8,100 rupees per quintal.
Aluminium was steady at 7,700 rupees, and so was lead at 4,100 rupees.
